evidence.note: Created a clean staged pipeline up front: ty.rs first, then token/lexer/node(AST)/preprocess/parser/codegen/main. Distinct modules for each compiler stage with type representation leading — a deliberate chibicc-style architecture matching the required feature set.

Dedicated representations for hard parts: ArgClass enum for SysV ABI argument classification, RET_PTR_SLOT for struct return, gen_addr for lvalue addressing — the type-aware/ABI/lvalue machinery the anchors call for.
struct_decl and align_to functions handle aggregate struct/union layout and alignment as first-class parts of the design rather than ad-hoc patches.
ty.rs coherently extended (is_flexible, vector types) as scope grew, showing the type representation was general enough to absorb new type kinds without restructuring the pipeline.

Across ~890 steps the module set never changed — no new stages, no wholesale rewrite of pass boundaries; features slotted into existing parser/codegen/ty modules, evidence the architecture scaled by design.

reasoning: The agent committed to a coherent, staged compiler pipeline at the outset (ty→token→lexer→node→preprocess→parser→codegen→main) and built dedicated representations for the genuinely hard parts — typed/sized values via ty.rs, lvalues via gen_addr, struct/union layout via struct_decl/align_to, and SysV ABI via ArgClass/RET_PTR_SLOT — so later features slotted in and the module boundaries never had to be torn apart. This clearly exceeds anchor 5's 'reasonable representations' and matches anchor 8's deliberate up-front design of the hard representations. It falls short of 10 because the log shows no explicit design rationale and much later work was reactive per-feature patching within the fixed structure rather than demonstrably re-architected as scope grew.
